JVHD.apk build provenance
repo:     Binkyo2013/JVHD-apk
commit:   a654f33 (fix: restore the missing Kotlin runtime and RawResponse$1;
          this file was updated in the commit right after it)
built:    2026-09-21T05:32:00Z (sandbox rebuild)
apk:      dist/JVHD.apk
sha256:   432566fb5caf5013832c2eda53670e64a263fc2d0d435bb8ff0ff8e62ed92ee6
size:     975782 bytes

This build SUPERSEDES the previous dist copy (sha256 037a167f..., built from
c6f8caf) - that copy crashed on launch because it contained no Kotlin
runtime at all. Verified: scripts/verify_dex_links.py run against the old
file reports 352 dangling references, including
  Lkotlin/jvm/internal/Intrinsics; and its member references,
  Lkotlin/jvm/internal/Ref$IntRef;, Lkotlin/Unit;, Lkotlin/UShort;,
  Lkotlin/io/path/PathsKt; -> readText/appendText/...,
  Lcom/JVHD/vip/RawResponse$1;
Run against this file it reports RESULT: PASSED (the DEX files link
completely).

== what was fixed ==
[1] Kotlin runtime missing from the APK (root cause of the instant exit)
    The app's own classes are compiled from Kotlin 1.8.22 and call the Kotlin
    standard library on every startup path (Intrinsics.checkNotNullParameter
    first of all), but classes.dex + classes2.dex shipped no kotlin/** classes
    besides a partial copy left in the decompiled smali/ tree. Android
    therefore threw NoClassDefFoundError inside MainActivity.onCreate before
    the first frame was drawn, which the system reports as "app closed".
    105 classes were restored from an authentic kotlin-stdlib-1.8.22 tree
    (universe: three repositories whose whole kotlin/** smali tree matches
    1.8.22; the class closure was computed with scripts/restore_kotlin_runtime.py
    until it reached a fixed point) and now live in smali_classes3/:
    kotlin/jvm/internal/Intrinsics, Ref, Ref$IntRef/ObjectRef/..., Unit,
    Lambda, Function0/1/2/3, DefaultConstructorMarker, TypeIntrinsics, UShort,
    UShortArray, KMappedMarker, TextStreamsKt, ArrayDeque, UnsignedKt, ...
    Provenance of every one of the 105 files: smali_classes3/RESTORED-CLASSES.txt.
[2] com.JVHD.vip.RawResponse$1 was undefined (second, latent defect)
    smali_classes2/com/JVHD/vip/RawResponse.smali instantiates it and callers
    in the DoH layer (Doh, DohHelper, FakeHttpURLConnection) would have died
    with NoClassDefFoundError on the first DoH lookup. No public source
    contains the class (checked upstream camiboj/PDoH and every Binkyo2013
    repository), so it was re-created by hand as a plain subclass of
    RawResponse with the exact constructor the call site uses:
      <init>(ILjava/lang/String;Ljavax/net/ssl/SSLSocket;Ljava/io/InputStream;)V
    It captures no additional state and overrides nothing.
[3] Startup failures are no longer silent
    smali_classes2/com/JVHD/vip/CrashLogger.smali (a Thread.UncaughtException
    Handler installed first thing in MainActivity.onCreate) now writes the
    full stack trace of any uncaught exception - including exceptions raised
    on the WebView JavaScript bridge thread - to logcat (tag JVHD-CRASH) and
    to jvhd-crash.txt in the app's external files directory, then delegates to
    the previous handler. It never exits or finishes the activity itself.

== toolchain ==
JDK:       openjdk version "25.0.2" 2026-01-20 LTS (jdk4py 25.0.2.1 runtime)
apktool:   2.9.3 - sha256 7956eb04194300ce0d0a84ad18771eebc94b89fb8d1ddcce8ea4c056818646f4
           (npm packages @postar/apktool-node and apk-revise ship it verbatim;
           GitHub release assets and the LFS CDN are unreachable here)
aapt2:     2.19-eng.20269 (prebuilt/linux/aapt2_64 extracted from the apktool
           jar by scripts/build-apk.sh itself)
framework: the framework reference shipped inside the apktool jar
zipalign:  scripts/zipalign.py -f -p 4 (no Android SDK build-tools in sandbox)
apksigner: 0.9 (standalone jar from the same npm package)
disassembler for cross-checks: none needed - scripts/verify_apk.py and
           scripts/verify_dex_links.py parse the DEX structures directly

== pipeline (exactly what ran - the repo's own script, unmodified) ==
  bash scripts/build-apk.sh            (JAVA_HOME=jdk4py, APKTOOL_JAR=<2.9.3>,
                                        APKSIGNER_JAR=<apksigner 0.9>)

  inside the script:
  java -jar apktool.jar b <staged project> -o JVHD-unsigned.apk --use-aapt2
      -> classes.dex (838 classes) + classes2.dex (10 classes)
         + classes3.dex (116 classes) + aapt2 resource link
  scripts/zipalign.py -f -p 4 JVHD-unsigned.apk JVHD.apk
      -> resources.arsc + lib/*.so STORED (apktool.yml doNotCompress),
         stored entries 4-aligned, *.so page (4096) aligned
  java -jar apksigner.jar sign --ks keystore/jvhd-debug.keystore
       --ks-pass pass:android --ks-key-alias jvhddebug --key-pass pass:android
  java -jar apksigner.jar verify --verbose --print-certs

== verification (scripts/verify_dex_links.py - RESULT: PASSED) ==
  classes.dex : dex v035, 838 classes, 1210 types, 10917 method ids
  classes2.dex: dex v035, 10 classes, 71 types, 165 method ids
  classes3.dex: dex v035, 116 classes, 344 types, 1152 method ids
  [1] dangling type references (964 classes defined, 1625 type ids)
      [ OK ] every non-platform type id is defined by the APK
  [2] dangling superclass/interface references
      [ OK ] every superclass/interface of every defined class is defined
             or is a platform class (java/javax/android/androidx/dalvik/...)
  [3] dangling member references (field/method ids owned by APK classes)
      [ OK ] 12235 field/method ids owned by APK classes all resolve
             (signature-level, walking the superclass/interface chain)
  This is the check that catches exactly the class of defect that made the
  previous dist copy crash: an APK that installs fine, starts, and dies with
  NoClassDefFoundError because a referenced class was never packaged.

== verification (scripts/verify_original_manifest.py - RESULT: PASSED) ==
  11/32 entries of the original APK byte-identical, 21 intentionally
  recompiled/renamed, 0 missing, 4 new (classes3.dex + 3 alignment/padding
  entries). All original assets, resource images, Kotlin builtins and both
  native libraries are preserved.

== additional audits run for this fix ==
  - reflective lookups: no "com/JVHD/..." or DoH class name appears as a
    string constant in any dex, so no class is loaded by name through
    Class.forName/loadClass reflection (would have been invisible to the
    linker check).
  - JavaScript bridge: all four bridge methods called from assets/*.js
    (proxyMedia, c0, d0, e0) exist in com.JVHD.vip.TizenBridge and are
    annotated @JavascriptInterface.
  - JNI: scripts/patch_btcore_jni.py --check - the renamed export
    Java_com_JVHD_vip_TizenBridge_n0 resolves in the .hash/.gnu.hash of both
    libbtcore.so ABIs.
  - startup path: MainActivity.onCreate (Kotlin) wraps its whole setup in
    try/catch -> showStartupError (logcat JVHD-CRASH + jvhd-crash.txt); there
    is no self-exit/close call path in the app (closeBinTVApplication() has
    exactly two call sites, both behind user dialogs).

== reproducibility ==
dist/JVHD.apk is byte-identical to a build of the commit above; rebuilding
that tree with the toolchain listed here reproduces
sha256 432566fb5caf5013832c2eda53670e64a263fc2d0d435bb8ff0ff8e62ed92ee6.

== NOT verified (no physical Android device available) ==
  - a real cold start on the user's device (install + tap to open)
  - the DoH/raw-HTTP path that exercises the re-created RawResponse$1
  - the renamed JNI export resolving on a real ART runtime (verified by the
    ELF hash simulation inside scripts/patch_btcore_jni.py, not by dlopen)
  - software-rendered WebView UI smoothness on affected devices

If anything still goes wrong at launch, the app now leaves evidence:
  adb logcat -s JVHD-CRASH
  adb shell cat /sdcard/Android/data/com.JVHD.vip/files/jvhd-crash.txt
